caption: Fade: sparks leaving trails that die away over about a second
why: Trails are what make motion read on LEDs: a moving dot with a tail looks like it is going somewhere. The trick is to keep last frame's picture, dim it a little, and draw the new frame on top. Fade is the dimming part - a colour times keep, named for the job it does after Previous.

keep sets how long the trails last: 0.9 fades to almost nothing in about a second, 0.98 lingers several seconds. Its neighbours: Scale is the same sum, named for any dimming; Previous and Previous at give the last frame to fade; Blur softens as well as keeping it.
steps: **Previous** gives this pixel's colour from last frame; it goes into Fade's **color**.
**keep** is 0.9: nine tenths of the light survives each frame, so a trail fades over about a second.
New light: a **Sparkle** (density 0.03, reseeded twelve times a second) in the **Palette**'s colour for its place.
A **Blend** in max mode keeps the brighter of the faded old picture and the new sparks: each spark flashes and fades over the next frames instead of vanishing.

try.label: Long trails
try.text: keep 0.98: the light lingers for seconds, so the sparks pile up into a glittering haze.

try.label: Short trails
try.text: keep 0.6: the light is gone in a few frames - a quick flicker.

try.label: No trails
try.text: keep 0: nothing of last frame survives - each spark lasts exactly one frame.
